incidents.cause: The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from the powerlines while landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during an attempted go-around, which resulted in a runway excursion.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control and his failure to compensate for wind conditions which resulted in a ground loop.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during takeoff, resulting in a runway excursion and ground loop
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing flare, which resulted in a collision with terrain, and a nose over.
The fatigue fracture of the No. 6 piston connecting rod, which resulted in a loss of engine power.
The student pilot's inadequate compensation for the crosswind, which resulted in a loss of directional control.
A loss of engine power due to carburetor icing as a result of the pilot's failure to use carburetor heat.

The fracture of a hydraulic brake line fitting due to incorrect installation of the brake line by the pilot/owner, which resulted in a loss of brake pressure and subsequent loss of directional control during the landing roll.
The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control, which resulted in impact with terrain near the runway.
The pilot's loss of directional control during the landing roll which resulted in a runway excursion and impact with terrain.
The pilot's loss of directional control for undetermined reasons.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during landing in crosswind conditions.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll, and excessive use of brakes, which resulted in a runway excursion and nose over.
The pilot’s failure to attain sufficient altitude during the initial climb to clear trees due to an encounter with windshear.
The malfunction of the propeller autofeather system after takeoff for undetermined reasons, which resulted in both propellers going into feather and a hard landing.
NONE.
An in-flight collision with a flock of birds while the airplane was descending through a cloud layer.
The pilot’s failure to maintain terrain clearance during takeoff for undetermined reasons.
An encounter with convectively-induced turbulence and icing, which resulted in an in-flight upset and a loss of airplane control.
A landing gear collapse due to the separation of the actuator pinion bearing support from the actuator, which resulted in the failure of the actuator shaft.
A total loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.

The total loss of engine power due to carburetor icing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to maintain a proper approach speed during the forced landing, which resulted in impact with trees.
The fatigue fracture of the nose gear upper torque link, which resulted in the separation of the torque link from the shock strut and a loss of directional control.

A total loss of engine power during the initial climb after takeoff for reasons that could not be determined because examination of the engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
The pilot's failure to attain the proper touchdown point on the runway, which resulted in a runway overrun and subsequent aircraft noseover.
The pilot’s failure to maintain adequate airspeed and airplane control during takeoff in high density altitude conditions, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.

The student pilot's inadequate preflight planning and failure to maintain clearance from rising terrain, which resulted in controlled flight into terrain. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of situational awareness.
The pilot's inadequate recovery from a bounced landing.
The pilot’s inadequate compensation for the gusting crosswinds.
The complete loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
The flight instructor's delayed remedial action, inadequate recovery from a bounced landing, and failure to attain/maintain adequate airspeed during an attempted go-around.
A loss of engine power in flight due to fuel exhaustion as a result of the pilot's inadequate fuel planning.
The pilot’s failure to use a pre-takeoff checklist, which resulted in the fuel selector being in the off position, and subsequent loss of engine power during takeoff.

The failure of the glider tow rope, which lodged in the glider's rudder and resulted in a hard landing. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's failure to properly secure the glider's aft canopy.
The pilot's inadequate clearance from a tree during an attempted off-field landing.
The pilot’s failure to maintain control of the glider during takeoff.
The pilot's loss of directional control during landing.
The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing and subsequent nose-over.
A collision with a large bird during approach.

The flight instructor’s delayed remedial action to prevent the airplane from hitting the hangar door. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's misuse of the airplane's throttle, and his incorrect use of the wheel brakes.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during landing in gusting crosswind conditions.

incidents.op: TRI ROTOR SPRAY AND CHEMICAL INC
incidents.cause: The pilot’s distracted attention and failure to maintain sufficient altitude to clear terrain while maneuvering in dark night conditions.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with objects.
The pilot's lapse in monitoring the airplane's speed during a low level aerial application maneuver and its subsequent stall during the maneuver.
The pilot misjudged his altitude which resulted in the airplane contacting a wire during the low altitude aerial application maneuver.

The noninstrument-rated pilot’s continued flight into an area of known rain with reduced visibility and his failure to maintain airplane control while maneuvering the airplane after entering these conditions.
A total loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
The air traffic controller not following Federal Aviation Administration directives to establish sequencing and spacing between aircraft operating to the same runway.
